title: vuln-secrets-playback-2026-03-27
content:
Meeting: Security engineering bridge call - vuln & secrets playback (informal notes)
Date: 2026-03-27
Facilitator: Aisha Kumar
Attendees: Aisha, Liam, Priya, Marcus, Sofia, Tomas (observability), Devlin (infra on-call)

Purpose: quick sync to close out the week on the recent vuln reports, triage outcomes, and the secrets scanning false-positive spike. Capture owners and short timelines — this is a lightweight working doc, not the final report.

Agenda:
- Quick status updates on active CVEs and internal findings
- Secrets scanning (gitleaks) noise and remediation cadence
- Threat modeling note: new onboarding flow (token exchange)
- Action item review and next steps

1) Vulnerability triage summary
- New inbound: dependency scanner flagged lodash-related prototype pollution in one internal build (reported by Dependabot + Snyk). Triage outcome: low-medium risk for our runtime images because we only use a small subset (no user-supplied templates).
  - Owner: Marcus Chen (eng-serv).
  - Short-term mitigation: pin to patched lodash version in build images; add transient patch step in Dockerfile. Target: 2026-03-30 (SEC-423).
  - Longer term: upgrade dependency policy in CI to fail on critical/important; add a weekly auto-bump job for minor/patch updates. (JIRA:SEC-423 linked).
- Public CVE referenced by third-party report affecting an in-house telemetry collector (libnet-utils CVE-2026-119). Triage: moderate severity due to potential data exfil risk if exploited in pipeline runners.
  - Mitigation: immediate isolation of collector, disable remote config until patched, blocker bug filed for infra rolling update. Owner: Devlin. ETA: 2026-03-28 for disable, 2026-04-02 for full patch rollout. (JIRA:SEC-447).
- Notes: we need better telemetry around which services expose admin endpoints — plan to add a short checklist for on-call before enabling any connector that talks to external repos. Tomas to add a dashboard tile by next sync.

2) Secrets scanning and leakage incidents
- Background: overnight spike of gitleaks alerts across several repos. Initial triage found 18 alerts; after manual review, 14 were false positives (build artifacts, minified bundles containing obfuscated tokens used strictly for mock/test), 4 were legitimate exposures (test keys accidentally committed to staging-config).
- Immediate remediation for legit exposures:
  - Rotate exposed staging keys and add ejection + revocation step in the CI pipeline. Owner: Priya Desai. Completed: 2026-03-27 17:45 (rotated keys, deployed config).
  - Incident ticket created and linked to deployment audit. Add postmortem draft. Owner: Priya. ETA for postmortem: 2026-04-02.
- False positive reduction plan:
  - Adjust gitleaks rules to ignore known test token patterns and minified build fingerprints; create an allowlist for test-only artifacts stored under /tests/fixtures. Owner: Liam. ETA: 2026-04-01.
  - Add a pre-commit hook template to the developer handbook and ship via dev-x repo. Owner: Sofia. ETA: 2026-04-08.
- Detection enhancements:
  - Investigate adding repository-level commit scanning in PR pipelines (run gitleaks on PR diffs only). Pros: fewer noisy alerts, faster feedback. Cons: might miss historical exposures. Decision: implement PR-diff scanning now + weekly full-repo run. Owner: Marcus. ETA: PR-diff 2026-04-05, full weeklies 2026-04-12.

3) Threat modeling — onboarding token exchange flow (quick notes)
- Context: product team for Private on-prem deployments is designing a new onboarding flow where customer infra exchanges a short-lived onboarding token with our control plane to bootstrap the agent. This increases attack surface for man-in-the-middle and token replay at initial handshake.
- Key risks identified:
  - Token interception during bootstrap if HTTPS mutual TLS not enforced.
  - Token replay if token lifetime is too long and there is no nonce/one-time-use mechanism.
  - Insufficient audit trail for initial provisioning (who initiated bootstrap).
- Proposed mitigations (agreed as a working baseline):
  - Require mTLS for all onboarding endpoints by default; fall back to token+challenge only for legacy customers with explicit risk sign-off. Owner: Tomas + infra. ETA: 2026-04-09 to land mTLS enforcement flags.
  - Use signed one-time tokens with embedded nonce and very short TTL (<= 5 minutes). Owner: Product + Applied ML infra. Prototype: 2026-04-02.
  - Log bootstrap events to immutable audit stream (append-only storage), redact tokens, and provide an operator-initiated replay check. Owner: Sofia. ETA: 2026-04-16.
- Outstanding questions for architecture:
  - Can we reuse the existing KMS-attested key registry for signing these onboarding tokens? Action: Aisha to sync with security research and platform cryptography.
  - For air-gapped on-prem installs, how will customer supply, verify, and rotate the root certs? Product to draft a minimal operator checklist.

4) Operational notes and follow-ups
- Canary rollback policy: we observed no vulns introduced by last week's canary, but we still need a clearly documented fallback plan for Dedicated pools. Action: add a quick start rollback runbook to Console docs. Owner: Devlin. ETA: 2026-04-06.
- Pager fatigue: multiple noisy low-severity alerts (esp. scanning) are causing blur in the rotation. Proposal: escalate only critical/urgent to SRE pager, others to a daily digest channel. Action: Liam to draft new alerting thresholds and present to SRE next Tuesday.
- Documentation: create a short "secrets handling for engineers" one-pager that covers pre-commit hooks, how to rotate keys, and whom to contact. Owner: Sofia. Draft due 2026-04-03.

5) Action items (concise)
- Marcus: patch lodash in build images + CI dependency policy (target 2026-03-30).
- Devlin: isolate telemetry collector, disable remote config, prepare rolling patch (disable done; patch ETA 2026-04-02).
- Priya: rotate staging keys, incident ticket + postmortem draft (rotation done; postmortem 2026-04-02).
- Liam: tune gitleaks rules + alert thresholds; draft new SRE alert thresholds (gitleaks rules 2026-04-01; alerts draft 2026-04-06).
- Sofia: pre-commit hook template, one-pager docs, audit stream logging design (hooks 2026-04-08; docs 2026-04-03; audit design 2026-04-16).
- Tomas: dashboard tile for admin-endpoint exposure + mTLS enforcement plan (dashboard by next sync; mTLS flags 2026-04-09).
- Aisha: sync with crypto on using KMS for onboarding token signing (meeting scheduled 2026-03-29).

6) Parking lot / questions
- Do we want a policy to revoke all long-lived service tokens quarterly? Cost of rotation vs. risk needs quick assessment. Suggest product/security joint session.
- Should we mark certain repos as "sensitive" to require mandatory code-owner approval for PRs that touch config files? Ops/Platform to propose an enforcement mechanism.

7) Next sync
- Tentative: 2026-04-03 bridge call (same channel). Goal: verify lodash patch rollout, gitleaks rule changes, and progress on onboarding mTLS.

Notes & tone: this doc is intentionally light on formality — captures conversation fragments, decisions, and owners. I'll convert the agreed items into JIRA tickets and link them here when created. If you have omissions, add comments in the Confluence draft or ping in #sec-eng.
